Rashi on Yevamot 41a:10:1.hebrew: ואח"כ מת אחיו הב' - ונפלה אחותה, ואסרתה לראשונה עליו משום אחות זקוקה, ואע"ג דעבד בה מאמר, כדתנן בפ' ארבעה אחין: ב"ה אומרים, אוי לו על אשתו ואוי לו על אשת אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:10:1.english: And afterward his second brother died - And her sister fell [before him for levirate marriage] and rendered the first [sister] forbidden to him as the sister of a woman bound by a levirate bond, even though he had performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] with her, as we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin: Beit Hillel say, "Woe to him on account of his wife, and woe to him on account of his brother's wife."

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:11:1.hebrew: ואח"כ מתה אשתו של שני אחריו - ונשארה בעלת מאמר זו:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:11:1.english: And afterward the wife of the second [brother] died after him - And this [woman who had received] ma'amar remained.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:13:1.hebrew: ר' אלעזר היא - בפרק ב"ש: המגרש את האשה והחזירה מותרת ליבם, רבי אלעזר אוסר. הואיל ועמדה עליו שעה אחת באיסור גרושת אח:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:13:1.english: It is Rabbi Elazar - In the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai [the Mishnah states]: One who divorces his wife and takes her back, she is permitted to the yavam; Rabbi Elazar forbids [her], since she stood before him for a single moment under the prohibition of a brother's divorcee.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:14:1.english: That at the time of falling [for levirate marriage] she was not suitable - For prior to [her] falling [before him] she had become forbidden to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:15:1.english: [If] his yevama dies - [This] refers to one who betroths the sister of his yevama.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:15:2.english: [She] performs ḥalitza - Like [the opinion of] Shmuel and Rav Assi.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:17:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי אלעזר - בפרק בית שמאי, אלא גבי מגרש אשה והחזירה, משום דמנפילה ואילך לא איתסרא עליה, ואיסור שבחיי אחיו לא מהני השתא, דליכא למימר "אין אני קורא בה בשעת נפילה", דלאו בשעת נפילה הואי. אבל בברייתא דמקדש אחות יבמתו, דמנפילה ואילך איתסרא עליה, והרי אין אני קורא בה בשעת זיקת יבום "יבמה יבא עליה" — לא פליגי:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:17:1.english: The Rabbis only disagree with Rabbi Elazar - in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai, regarding [the case of] one who divorces [his] wife and takes her back, because from [the time of] falling [for levirate marriage] and onward she was not forbidden to him, and a prohibition that [existed] during his brother's lifetime is not effective now, since one cannot say "I do not apply [it] to her at the time of falling," for [the prohibition] was not at the time of falling. However, in the baraita of one who betroths the sister of his yevama, where from [the time of] falling and onward she became forbidden to him, and behold one cannot apply to her at the time of the levirate bond [the verse] "her brother-in-law shall go in unto her" — they do not disagree.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:18:1.english: [She] may not perform chalitzah - [It] explains the reason in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:18:2.hebrew: בתולות ובעולות ארוסות ונשואות - בגמרא בעי, מאי הפרש איכא בין בתולות לארוסות, בין נשואות לבעולות:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:18:2.english: Virgins and non-virgins, betrothed and married [women] - In the Gemara, [it] asks: What difference is there between virgins and betrothed [women], [and] between married [women] and non-virgins?

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:1.hebrew: הנשואות יתארסו - דטעמא משום להבחין בין זרע ראשון לזרע שני הוא, שלא תלד ספק בן ט' לראשון, ספק בן ז' לאחרון. ובאירוסין ליכא למימר הכי:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:1.english: The married women may be betrothed - For the reason [for waiting] is to distinguish between the seed of the first [husband] and the seed of the second [husband], so that she will not give birth to [a child of] uncertain [paternity] — [either] a nine-month [child] of the first or a seven-month [child] of the second. And regarding betrothal, one cannot say this.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:2.hebrew: והארוסות ינשאו - מיד, דהא לא איעברא מן הראשון:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:2.english: And the betrothed women may marry - Immediately, for she did not become pregnant from the first [husband].

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:3.hebrew: חוץ מארוסה שביהודה - דתנן פרק קמא דכתובות (דף יב.): ביהודה היו מייחדים החתן והכלה קודם כניסתן לחופה, כדי שיהא לבו גס בה, כלומר רגיל ומצחק עמה, שלא יהיו בושין זה מזה בבעילת מצוה. הלכך, חיישינן דלמא בעיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:19:3.english: Except for a betrothed woman in Judea - As we learned in a Mishnah in the first chapter of Ketubot (12a): In Judea, they would seclude the groom and the bride prior to their entry into the marriage canopy so that he would be familiar with her — that is to say, accustomed to [her] and playful with her — so that they would not be shy of one another during the mitzvah-intercourse. Therefore, we are concerned lest he cohabited [with her].

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:1:1.hebrew: הך דאזלא בהדה לבי דינא - כשלאה חולצת, מוליכה אחותה עמה לב"ד, וכ"ע לא ידעי הי מנייהו יבמתו, ואיכא דסבר דלרחל חלץ. וכי נסיב צרת רחל — דהיינו צרת קרובת חלוצתו — אמרי צרת חלוצתו נסיב, דאינהו סברי שרחל וצרתה נשי אחיו הוו, שהרי חלץ לרחל:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:1:1.english: That [woman] who goes with her to court - When Leah performs ḥalitza, she brings her sister [Rachel] with her to court, and not everyone knows which of them is his yevamah, so there are those who think that he performed ḥalitza for Rachel. And when he marries Rachel's rival wife — which is the rival wife of his ḥalutza's relative — they will say he married the rival wife of his ḥalutza, for they think that Rachel and her rival wife were his brother's wives, since he performed ḥalitza for Rachel.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:1:2.hebrew: האי דלא אזלא בהדה לבי דינא - כשהיבמה חולצת, אין צרתה הולכת עמה. הלכך, כי נסיב אחות צרה, לא אמרינן אחות חלוצתו נסיב:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:1:2.english: This [woman] who does not go with her to court - When the yevamah performs chalitzah, her rival wife does not go with her. Therefore, when he marries the sister of a rival wife, we do not say [that] he is marrying the sister of his chalutzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:20:1.hebrew: כל הנשים יתארסו - רבי יוסי אנשואות קאי, והכי (קא"ל ר' יהודה): כל הנשים נשואות יתארסו כדקאמרת, ולא גזרינן אירוסין אטו נשואין; ומיהו בהא פליגנא עלך, שלא חלקת בין אלמנה לגרושה, והתרת אלמנה ליארס בתוך ימי אבלה. ואנא סבירא לי: אלמנה מן הנשואין לא תארס כל שלשים ימי אבלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:20:1.english: All the women may be betrothed - Rabbi Yosei is referring to [previously] married women, and this is what [he says to] Rabbi Yehudah: "All married women may be betrothed, as you say, and we do not decree [a prohibition against] betrothal on account of marriage; however, in this [matter] I disagree with you, in that you did not distinguish between a widow and a divorcee, and you permitted a widow to be betrothed during the days of her mourning. Whereas I hold [that] a widow from marriage may not be betrothed [during] all thirty days of her mourning."

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:2:1.hebrew: ולא מתייבמת - דהויא לה אחות חלוצתו. ומיהו מחליצה לא מפטרא, דמדאוריית' רמיא קמיה, ואע"ג דאחותה קיימת, דאחות חלוצה אינה אלא מדברי סופרים:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:2:1.english: But she may not enter into levirate marriage - Because she is the sister of his ḥalutza [the woman with whom he performed ḥalitza]. However, she is not exempt from ḥalitza, because by Torah law she falls before him [for levirate marriage], even though her sister is alive, since [the prohibition against] the sister of a ḥalutza is only by rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:2:2.english: And similarly, one who divorced [his wife] - In the Gemara, it asks: What [is meant by] "and similarly"?

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:2:3.hebrew: פטורה - אף מן החליצה, דיוצאה משום אחות אשה, הואיל ואשתו קיימת, ואחות גרושה מדברי תורה, דכתיב (ויקרא י״ח:י״ח) "עליה בחייה" — כל שבחייה:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:2:3.english: Exempt - Even from chalitzah, for she is exempt on account of [being] a wife's sister, since his [divorced] wife is still alive, and [the prohibition of] a divorcee's sister is biblical, as it is written (Leviticus 18:18): "beside her in her lifetime" — [meaning] as long as she is alive.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:1.hebrew: שומרת יבם שקדש - אחד מן האחין את אחותה, לאחר שנפלה זו לפניהם והוזקקה לכולן:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:1.english: A widow waiting for her yavam, where [one] betrothed - one of the brothers [betrothed] her sister, after this [woman] fell before them [for levirate marriage] and became bound to all of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:2.hebrew: המתן - מלכנוס, דקא פגעת באחות זקוקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:2.english: Wait - from entering [into marriage], for you are encountering the sister of a [woman] bound [by a levirate bond].

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:3.hebrew: עד שיעשה מעשה - שיכנסו האחין את היבמה או יחלצו, ותעקר זיקתה ממך:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:3:3.english: Until [he] performs an act - That the brothers consummate levirate marriage with the yevama or perform chalitzah, and [thereby] her levirate bond will be uprooted from you.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:4:1.hebrew: מתה היבמה יכנוס את אשתו - דאפילו כנסה ומתה, מותר באחותה:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:4:1.english: [If] the yevama died, he may marry his wife - For even if he had married her and she died, he is permitted [to marry] her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:4:2.english: [If] the yavam died - and no brother remained to him except this one.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:4:3.hebrew: ואת אשת אחיו בחליצה - אבל יבומי לא, דאחות גרושתו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:4:3.english: And his brother's wife with chalitzah - But [he may] not [perform] yibum, for she is the sister of his divorcée.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:7:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira] - For there is zikah [a levirate bond], and it is strong [enough] to forbid [his betrothed] to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:8:1.hebrew: מהו ביבמתו - מי אמרינן כיון דמתה פקע איסור אחות אשה ושריא, או דלמא אע"ג דפקע איסור אחות אשה, קם עליה באיסור אשת אח? הואיל ונאסרה עליו שעה אחת בשעה שהיתה זקוקה ליבם, ואין אני קורא בה "יבמה יבא עליה", הרי היא כאשת אח שיש לה בנים ואסורה עולמית עליו:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:8:1.english: What is [the law] with regard to his yevama - Do we say [that] since she [his wife] died, the prohibition of a wife's sister has lapsed and she [the yevama] is permitted, or perhaps, even though the prohibition of a wife's sister has lapsed, the prohibition of a brother's wife remains upon her? Since she was forbidden to him for one moment at the time she became bound to the yavam, and I cannot apply to her [the verse], "her yavam shall consummate [levirate marriage] with her," she is like a brother's wife who has children and is forever forbidden to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:9:1.hebrew: מ"ט דרב - דשרי? הרי נאסרה עליו שעה אחת:
Rashi on Yevamot 41a:9:1.english: What is Rav’s reasoning - That he permits [her]? Behold, she was forbidden to him for one moment.

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:9:2.english: Who was permitted - at the time she fell [before the yavam for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 41a:9:3.english: [She] became forbidden - When this [yavam] betrothed her sister.

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:10:1.hebrew: עשה בה מופנה מאמר - לא אצטריך אלא לאפוקי מב"ש, דאמר (לעיל יבמות דף כט.) מאמר קונה קנין גמור. אי נמי, נקט "עשה בה מאמר" לאשמועינן דאע"ג דאין זיקת השניה גמורה, אפילו הכי אוסרת את זו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:10:1.english: "The bachelor performed levirate betrothal (ma'amar) with her" - [This] was only necessary to exclude [the view of] Beit Shammai, who say (above, Yevamot 29a) [that] ma'amar effects a complete acquisition. Alternatively, [the baraita] stated "performed ma'amar with her" to teach us that even though the levirate bond of the second [sister] is not complete, nevertheless she prohibits this [first] one.

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:12:1.hebrew: ואמאי תיהוי יבמה שהותרה כו' - תימה, דלא פריך מהך ברייתא לרב בריש פרק ארבעה אחין (לעיל יבמות דף כח.), ולישני דרבי אלעזר היא כדמשני הכא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:12:1.english: But why should she be [like] a yevama who was permitted, etc. - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not raise a difficulty from this baraita against Rav at the beginning of the chapter Arba'ah Achin (above, Yevamot 28a), and [then] answer that it is [the view of] Rabbi Elazar, just as it answers here.

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:14:1.hebrew: הדר אמר אימור דאמר רבי אלעזר כו' - אכתי הוה מצי למימר דטעמא דר' אלעזר כדמפרש לקמן בפרק ב"ש (יבמות דף קט. ושם), אבל בהך ברייתא דלמא לא פליגי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:14:1.english: He then said: One could say that Rabbi Elazar said, etc. - He still could have said that Rabbi Elazar's reason is as [the Gemara] explains later in the chapter Beit Shammai (Yevamot 109a and there), whereas in this baraita perhaps they do not disagree.

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:1:1.hebrew: הך דאזלא בהדה לבי דינא - פי' בקונטרס: כשלאה חולצת, מוליכה רחל אחותה עמה לב"ד, ואיכא דסברי שרחל חלצה, ולהכי אסורה גם צרתה, אפילו שתיהן נשואות לנכרי, דאינהו סברי שרחל וצרתה נשי אחיו היו, שהרי חלץ לרחל. ותימה גדולה פירש! דהא תנן במתניתין "ובאחותה בזמן שהיא קיימת", הא מתה — שריא; ותנן נמי לקמן (יבמות דף מט.): "חלץ לה ומתה — מותר באחותה", ואמאי? והא סברי שלאחותה חלץ! ועוד, דתנן: האחין מותרין, אע"ג דאזלי בהדיה לבי דינא. ועוד, דלא מיתסר צרה אלא דוקא במצוה, כדאמרינן בפ' קמא (לעיל יבמות ח.); ולעיל בריש ארבעה אחין (יבמות דף כז. ושם), גבי "התחיל באחיות", מייתי לה למתני' דהכא, דהיינו ששניהן נשואות לאחיו. ופ"ה יש לישב קצת בנשואה לאחיו ולא לנכרי. ונרא' לר"י דגרסי': "הא דאזלא בהדיה לבי דינא" — פי', שהולכת לחלוץ; וכיון דחלצה, דמיא לגרושה טפי, ואסרו גם צרת קרובתה כנשואה לאחין, דדמיא לצרת ערוה. אבל כשחולצת צרת לאה ולא לאה — לא דמיא לאה לגרושה, ואפילו רחל, שהיא קרובת צרת חלוצה, שריא. ויש ספרים דלא גרסי לא "בהדיה" ולא "בהדה", אלא "הא דאזלא לבי דינא והא דלא אזלא":
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:1:1.english: That [woman] who goes together with her to court - Rashi explained: When Leah performs ḥalitza, she brings her sister Rachel with her to court, and there are [those who see this and] think that Rachel performed ḥalitza; therefore her rival wife is also forbidden, even if both of them are married to an unrelated man, because they think that Rachel and her rival wife were the wives of his brother, since he performed ḥalitza with Rachel. And this is a great astonishment [that he] explained [so]! For we learned in the Mishnah: "and [he is forbidden] to her sister while she is alive" — [implying that] if she died, she is permitted; and we also learned later (Yevamot 49a): "[If] he performed ḥalitza with her and she died, he is permitted to her sister." Yet why [should she be permitted]? Surely people think that he performed ḥalitza with her sister! Furthermore, we learned [in the Mishnah] that the brothers [of the yavam] are permitted [to the ḥalutza's relatives], even though they go together with him to court. Furthermore, a rival wife is only forbidden specifically in [a case of] a mitzvah [i.e., levirate marriage], as we say in the first chapter (above, Yevamot 8a); and above, at the beginning of [the chapter] Arba'ah Aḥin (Yevamot 27a and there [in Tosafot]), regarding "He began with the sisters," [the Gemara] cites our Mishnah here, [which implies] that both of them are married to his brothers. And Rashi's explanation can be reconciled somewhat [if it refers] to [a woman] married to his brother, and not to an unrelated man. And it appears to Ri that we read [the text as]: "This [woman] who goes with him [bahadeih] to court" — meaning, who goes to perform ḥalitza; and since she performed ḥalitza, she resembles a divorcee more [strongly], so they also forbade the rival wife of her relative when [that relative was] married to [one of the] brothers, because she resembles the rival wife of a forbidden relative [ervah]. However, when Leah's rival wife performs ḥalitza and not Leah, Leah does not resemble a divorcee, and even Rachel, who is the relative of the ḥalutza's rival wife, is permitted. And there are texts that read neither "with him" [bahadeih] nor "with her" [bahadah], but rather: "This [woman] who goes to court, and this [woman] who does not go."

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:20:1.hebrew: רבי יוסי אומר כל הנשים יתארסו - בעירובין (דף מז.) פי' בקונט' דאפילו ארוסות, דוקא יתארסו, אבל ינשאו לא, דגזר רבי יוסי ארוסה אטו נשואה. ואין נראה, דאי גרס בברייתא דרדופה "רבי יוסי מתיר ליארס ולינשא מיד", א"כ קשיא דרבי יוסי אדרבי יוסי: דהכא גזר אפילו ארוסה אטו נשואה, כ"ש דהוה ליה למיגזר נשואה רדופה אטו שאינה רדופה! ואפילו גרס בברייתא דרדופה "רבי יהודה", מ"מ קשיא: דהיכי מוכח בפרק מי שהוציאוהו (ג"ז שם) ובגמ' דיחידאה פליג עליה מברייתא דרדופה, ותנא קמא דמתניתין הוא ר"מ? דלמא ר"מ דרדופה הוא כר' יוסי דמתניתין, דלא שרי אלא ליארס, אבל לינשא לא; ו"צריכות להמתין שלשה חדשים" דקאמר ר"מ, היינו מלינשא, אבל ליארס מיד שרי! ואף על גב דקתני סתמא "צריכות להמתין", הכי נמי קתני בפרק ד' אחין (לעיל יבמות דף לה. ושם) גבי גיורת ושבויה ואנוסה ומפותה "צריכות להמתין" סתמא, דברי רבי יהודה; וע"כ היינו דוקא לינשא, דליארס אפי' נשואה שרי הכא ר"י! ועוד: היכי מוכח בגמ' דהדר ביה ר' יוחנן ממתני' דכרמא, דקתני "כולן צריכות להמתין"? דלמא לינשא קאמר, אבל ליארס שרי! ונראה כמו שפי' רש"י כאן, דרבי יוסי שרי נמי ארוסה לינשא, ולא פליג ארבי יהודה אלא באיבול לחודיה. ומיהו, מה שהביא ראיה דשמעינן לרבי יוסי דמיקל בהבחנה טפי מרבי יהודה בסוף פרק ד' אחין (ג"ז שם), אינה ראיה: דדלמא בגיורת ואנוסה מיקל משום דמתהפכת שלא תתעבר, כדאמרינן לעיל (יבמות דף לה.), אבל לעולם גזר ארוסה אטו נשואה. ומברייתא דרדופה היה יכול לדקדק, אי גרס בה ר' יוסי: דלא גזר אפי' נשואה רדופה אטו שאין רדופה, כ"ש דלא גזר ארוסה אטו נשואה. והא דפסיק רבי יוחנן כר' יוסי ולא נקט ר' יהודה, כיון דשניהם שוין: משום שבא לפסוק כרבי יוסי גם באיבול, או נקט ר' יוסי כדפי' בקונטרס, משום דנימוקו עמו. וא"ת: כשמגיה בגמרא (לקמן יבמות מג.) "אימא: רבי יוסי אומר כל הנשים ינשאו", ופריך "ולית ליה לרבי יוסי להבחין?", ומאי קשיא ליה? נימא ד"כל הנשים" לאו דוקא, ואארוסות דוקא קאי ולא אנשואות, דמעיקרא נמי לא הוי "כל" דוקא, דלא הוי קאי אלא אנשואות, דארוסות שרי אפילו לינשא! וי"ל דלא דמי: דהשתא הוי "כל" דוקא וקאי שפיר בין אארוסות בין אנשואות, אלא שהדיוק — דמשמע "יתארסו אין, ינשאו לא" — לא קאי אכל נשים אלא אנשואות לחוד, אבל פשטא דמתניתין אכל נשים קאי. אבל קשה לר"ת: דקתני לקמן בברייתא "וכולן לא ינשאו עד שיהו להם שלשה חדשים", משמע אפילו ארוסות, כמו "כל הנשים", ודוחק לחלק בין "וכולן" ל"כל הנשים"! ואר"ת דגרס בברייתא דרדופה "רבי יוסי מתיר ליארס", ול"ג "לינשא", וגזר ר' יוסי ארוסה אטו נשואה. ודוחק הוא למחוק הספרים, דבכולהו גרס "לינשא"; ועוד, דליארס אפילו נשואה שרי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:20:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: All of the women may be betrothed - In Eruvin (47a), [Rashi] explained in the Kunteres that even betrothed women [may] only be betrothed [again], but they may not be married, because Rabbi Yosei decreed [prohibiting the marriage of] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman. But this does not seem [correct], for if one reads in the baraita of a redufah [a woman living apart from her husband] "Rabbi Yosei permits [her] to be betrothed and to be married immediately," if so, [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei contradicts [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei: for here he decreed even [regarding] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman, [so] all the more so should he have decreed [regarding] a married woman who was estranged (redufah) on account of one who was not estranged! And even if one reads in the baraita of a redufah "Rabbi Yehudah," nevertheless it is difficult: for how does [the Gemara] prove in the chapter Mi Shehotzi'uhu (also there [Eruvin 47a]) and in [our] Gemara that an individual [Tanna] disagrees with him from the baraita of a redufah, and [that] the Tanna Kamma of our Mishnah is Rabbi Meir? Perhaps Rabbi Meir of [the baraita of] a redufah is like Rabbi Yosei of our Mishnah, who only permits [her] to be betrothed, but not to be married; and "they must wait three months" that Rabbi Meir says means from marrying, whereas to be betrothed immediately is permitted! And even though it teaches without qualification "they must wait," so too it teaches in the chapter Arba'ah Achin (above, Yevamot 35a and there) regarding a convert, a captive, a violated woman, and a seduced woman "they must wait" without qualification, [as] the words of Rabbi Yehudah; and perforce that refers specifically to marrying, since to be betrothed, Rabbi Yehudah permits here even a married woman! And furthermore: how does [the Gemara] prove in the Gemara that Rabbi Yochanan retracted from the Mishnah of Kerma, which teaches "all of them must wait"? Perhaps it is speaking of marrying, whereas to be betrothed is permitted! Rather, it appears [correct] as Rashi explained here, that Rabbi Yosei also permits a betrothed woman to be married, and he only disagrees with Rabbi Yehudah regarding mourning (ivul) alone. However, [the fact] that he brought a proof [from] that we have heard that Rabbi Yosei is more lenient regarding distinguishing [between husbands] than Rabbi Yehudah at the end of the chapter Arba'ah Achin (also there) is not a proof: for perhaps he is lenient regarding a convert and a violated woman because she turns over [after intercourse] so that she does not conceive, as we say above (Yevamot 35a), whereas in general he did decree [prohibiting] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman. Rather, from the baraita of a redufah he could have inferred [this], if one reads "Rabbi Yosei" in it: since he did not decree even [regarding] a married woman who was estranged (redufah) on account of one who was not estranged, all the more so did he not decree [regarding] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman. And as to why Rabbi Yochanan ruled like Rabbi Yosei and did not mention Rabbi Yehudah, since both of them are equal [on this matter]: [it is] because he came to rule like Rabbi Yosei also regarding mourning, or he mentioned Rabbi Yosei, as [Rashi] explained in the Kunteres, because "his reasoning is with him." And if you say: When [the Gemara] emends [the Mishnah] in the Gemara (below, Yevamot 43a) [to read] "Say: Rabbi Yosei says all of the women may be married," and asks "And does Rabbi Yosei not hold [of the need] to distinguish?" — what is its difficulty? Let us say that "all of the women" is not exact, and refers specifically to betrothed women and not to married women, for originally too "all" was not exact, since it only referred to married women, as betrothed women are permitted even to be married! And one can say that it is not comparable: for now [without the emendation] "all" is exact and refers well both to betrothed women and to married women, except that the inference — which implies "they may be betrothed, yes; they may be married, no" — does not refer to all women, but only to married women alone, whereas the plain reading of the Mishnah refers to all women. However, it is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: for it teaches below in a baraita "and all of them may not be married until three months have passed for them," which implies even betrothed women, just like "all of the women," and it is forced to distinguish between "and all of them" and "all of the women"! And Rabbeinu Tam says that he reads in the baraita of a redufah "Rabbi Yosei permits [her] to be betrothed," and we do not read "to be married," and [thus] Rabbi Yosei decreed [prohibiting the marriage of] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman. [However,] it is forced to erase [the text of] the books, for in all of them it reads "to be married"; and furthermore, to be betrothed is permitted even [for] a married woman:

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:4:1.hebrew: יוציא את אשתו בגט - בפ' ארבעה אחין (לעיל יבמות כט.) לא בעי למימר ד"זו היא" למעוטי הך דהכא, דפשע, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:4:1.english: He must divorce his wife with a bill of divorce - In the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (above, Yevamot 29a), [the Gemara] did not need to say that "This is" [comes] to exclude this [case] here, because he acted negligently, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:8:1.hebrew: מתה אשתו מותר ביבמתו - ומתני' דקתני "מתה יבמתו", ולא נקט "מתה אשתו" דהוי רבותא טפי — איידי דבעי למיתני "מת היבם", תנא נמי "מתה היבמה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:8:1.english: If his wife died, he is permitted to his yevama - And [as for] the Mishnah, which teaches, "If his yevama died," and did not state, "If his wife died," which would be a greater novelty — since [the Tanna] wanted to teach, "If the yavam died," he also taught, "If the yevama died."

Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:9:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דרב משום דהוי יבמה שהותרה - ואע"פ דבפ' ארבעה אחין (יבמות דף כז:) שרי רב אפילו לא הותרה לכתחלה, דקאמר: "מתה הראשונה מותר בשניה" — היינו דוקא בזיקה דרבנן; אבל הכא, אחות אשה דאורייתא, דוקא משום דהותרה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 41a:9:1.english: "What is Rav's reasoning? Because she is a yevama who was permitted" - Even though in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 27b) Rav permits [levirate marriage] even where she was not permitted initially — as he says: "If the first one died, he is permitted to the second one" — that is specifically regarding a rabbinic levirate bond; however, here, [where the prohibition of] a wife's sister is by Torah law, [she is permitted] specifically because she was [initially] permitted.
